positioning: Custom-built sound systems for high-end architectural spaces — designed, built, and tuned entirely in-house.
visionHead: To reintroduce sound as a physical, spatial experience — designed to move correctly within architectural space.
visionBody: At Eliyah Acoustic, we build every system as a custom, hand-crafted piece designed specifically for its space — and we tune it ourselves, in-house, as an integral part of the service. This is how each system is brought into full harmony with the space it lives in.
coreHead: Sound is not a fixed standard. It is personal, contextual, and shaped by space.
coreSub: A system is defined by its relationship with the room. We design, build, and tune systems that are:

coreItems.text: Custom-built, from the ground up, for the specific space
Tuned in-house, by us, through listening — never through presets

coreClose: The loudspeaker is not the product. It is part of a larger acoustic composition.
principleHead: A system is successful when it changes behavior.
principleBody: It is not defined by how it sounds, but by what it creates in the space. When it is tuned correctly:

scopeHead: Projects begin around ₪70,000 and can reach ₪400,000 and above.
studioHead: Eliyah Acoustic approaches sound as something that is shaped within space.
studioA: Our work is built on years of listening — to systems that were not only heard, but physically experienced. From controlled studio environments to large-scale club systems designed by Richard Long, our understanding of sound was formed through direct experience with its physical presence.
studioB: We work from reference — a clear internal understanding of how sound should behave within a space. Tuning is a central part of our process, and it is always carried out by us, in-house, as part of the service. It is not about correction, but about refinement and alignment. The result is a system that is not only heard, but fully experienced.
approachHead: The loudspeaker is not the system. It is one component within a larger acoustic structure.
approachBody: Most sound systems are designed as independent objects, and later placed into a space. In practice, sound is always shaped by the room. The space defines how it behaves — how it reflects, builds, and disperses. For this reason, each system begins with the room itself:
approachClose: From there, we develop and build the system in-house to work within these conditions. This approach allows sound to sit naturally in the space, with presence, balance, and stability.
expHead: The goal is not clarity alone, nor volume, nor technical precision. It is engagement.
expBody: Not because the sound is louder, but because it aligns with the body. At that point, the listener stops analyzing and starts responding. Sound becomes physical. It becomes immersive. And it holds its presence within the space.
percHead: Sound is experienced differently in every space and by every listener.
percBody: A system that performs well in one environment may behave differently in another. Each project is therefore approached individually. The system is developed in relation to the room and the listener. The process includes continuous adjustment and refinement, carried out by us, until the system feels natural within the space and aligned with how the client experiences sound.
matBody: Materials are selected not only for their structural qualities, but for the way they influence sound behavior. Wood, in particular, is used for its ability to support natural resonance and controlled diffusion. Enclosures, waveguides, and horn structures are designed and built by us to control dispersion, timing, and energy distribution — each system developed as a visible element within the space.
appHead: Systems are developed for private residences and select high-end public environments.
appBody: Each project is designed to support both focused listening and a natural flow of movement within the space. The system becomes an integral part of how the space is experienced and used.
maniHead: Sound is not fixed. It is shaped.
maniA: By space, material, and placement — and by the way it is experienced. A system cannot exist independently from the room. It is defined by it. Every surface affects it. Every proportion shifts it. Every decision leaves a trace.
maniB: We design and build systems that belong to their space. Built in relation to architecture. Developed through listening. Refined through tuning — always performed by us, in-house. What matters is how sound moves, how it settles, and how it holds presence within the room.
maniClose: When alignment is achieved, sound becomes physical. It is no longer observed. It is experienced.
aboutA: Our understanding of sound was formed early, in a period when sound systems were built from separate components — each with a defined role and frequency range. This way of working trained our ear to listen in layers.
aboutB: Our team’s first professional experience involved building crossover networks within one of Israel’s leading audio environments. Over time, we built more than a thousand of them, developing a precise understanding of frequency distribution, system balance, and acoustic behavior. From there, our work expanded into the design and tuning of sound environments in Israel and across Europe.
aboutQuote: “In one residential project, during a classical music listening session, a client described being able to perceive the exact position of the violinist within the space.”
aboutQuoteSub: This level of spatial definition is not achieved through equipment alone. It is the result of alignment — between system, space, and perception.
